public.title: Maximum Width of Binary Tree
public.description: Return the maximum width of any tree level, counting missing positions between its first and last non-null node as if the tree were complete. Empty trees have width 0. Tree depth is at most 40; the resulting width is a safe integer. Trees use compact breadth-first arrays: the first value is the root; each non-null node consumes the next two entries as left and right children. Null marks a missing child; trailing nulls may be omitted. Empty arrays mean no tree. Values are integers from -10000 to 10000, with at most 200 nodes.
hints: Track complete-tree position indices at each level.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and solutions, 2026. Adapted from a standard algorithmic problem; no third-party exercise text used.

explanation: Normalize positions by the first index of each level to avoid needless growth, then propagate doubled positions to children. O(n) time.
